newsitem.title: USA: DSP Group adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: DSP Group adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: DSP Group Inc said on Thursday that its board had adopted a Rights Agreement that would give DSPG shareholders a dividend in the form of preferred stock purchase rights.

The company said the rights become exercisable 10 business days after someone acquires beneficial ownership of 15 percent or more of its outstanding common stock or begins a tender or exchange to acquire such an amount.

"The rights agreement is designed to assure that DSPG's stockholders receive equal treatment in the event of any proposed takeover of DSPG, and to guard against partial tender offers, squeeze-outs and other abusive tactics to gain control of DSPG that could impair the board's ability to represent stockholders' interests fully," the company said in a statement.
It said one right for each share of common stock would be distributed to stockholders of record as of June 10, 1997.
Each right will let holders buy one one-thousandth of a share of Series A Preferred Stock at an initial exercise price of $70, the company said.
The company said the rights will expire at the close of business June 5, 2007.
